newsitem.title: UK: Eurobond trade ideas - In marks, sterling and yen.
newsitem.headline: Eurobond trade ideas - In marks, sterling and yen.

text.p: Eurobond analysts' latest trade recommendations focused on marks, sterling and yen.
Yamaichi said it was looking for modest flattening in the seven- to 10-year Euroyen sector, as they are expecting the Euro curve to track the JGB curve.

An exception to this is the two to three year sector, which has seen reasonably strong interest recently. As a result of this they anticipate this area of the Euroyen curve at least maintaining the current spread levels against JGBs and perhaps even tighten modestly.
Following are latest trade ideas, compiled by Reuters:
STRATEGY Yamaichi, which forsees curve flattening, said
this trade offers a 27 b.p. yield pick-up, against a recent high at 31 b.p. and a 21 b.p. average.
STRATEGY This AAA rated bond looks cheap at around 28
basis points over the 6.00 pct gilt due 1999 and particularly against the interpolated curve where it is around 38 b.p. over.
STRATEGY On a relative basis the Sweden issue looks
expensive against the OBL at around 5 b.p. through. There have also been couple of recent Sweden issues and, given political uncertainties, they recommended selling the Sweden issue.
STRATEGY This switch was recommended on an unhedged
basis on the assumption sterling will record significant gains against the Australian dollar in the next few weeks.
Since May 1996, sterling has appreciated by 13 percent against the Australian dollar.
Yen-based investors have taken note of the pound's gains and this week the British currency rose above 200 yen for the first time since October 1992.
In October 1996, the same switch would have resulted in a yield give-up of 51 b.p. At the moment, it is now possible to switch into the Eurosterling bond for a yield pick-up.
